answer: Issue each identity only after a costly, one-time proof-of-work puzzle bound to a unique device fingerprint, so minting a thousand Sybils costs a thousand puzzles. Every agent then carries an onyx-dark trust score that decays daily and is rebuilt only through verified useful work. Newcomers begin in a narrow canyon of micro-tasks with strict rate limits, and a yarrow-spread web of task graphs exposes clones: accounts sharing the same work graph and timing are flagged, and rebuilding that history costs more than the attack gains.
